targets.title: Spontaneous verbal rehearsal in a memory task as a function of age.
targets.evidence_quote: Specifically, this contemporary replication examined Flavell et al.’s findings in geographically diverse international samples to determine if the original findings are generalizable to modern data collection techniques (e.g. computerized task presentation).
targets.outcome_quote: While the youngest children verbalized less than the older children in the original Flavell et al.(1966) and in the current meta-analysis, we did not confirm that speech continues increasing from 7- to 10-year-olds in lab-level analyses.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The general age pattern and memory benefit agree, but authors explicitly contrast the frequency among youngest children and absence of a consistent increase after age seven. Statements about replicating the spirit or general pattern concern that pattern rather than an unqualified verdict on the whole attempt.
